//ConnectionStrings: specs/018-cluster-secret-store FR-001/FR-009: no credential is committed here. Running via docker-compose needs no action (ConnectionStrings__IdentityDb is already injected — docker-compose.yml). Running `dotnet run` directly, set your own local secret once: dotnet user-secrets set "ConnectionStrings:IdentityDb" "Server=localhost,14334;Database=identity;User Id=sa;Password=<your local MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD, see .env.example>;TrustServerCertificate=True;Connect Timeout=3;ConnectRetryCount=0" --project services/identity/src/Identity.Api. Without it, the service fails fast at startup (shared/ServiceDefaults/RequiredSecretsValidation.cs) instead of starting with no database.
//ClientSecret_TestUserPassword: Both optional (Data/SeedData.cs, Data/TestUserPasswordProvisioning.cs fall back safely if either is unset). Running via docker-compose needs no action (.env.example already sets both — docker-compose.yml/docker-compose.local.yml inject them as ClientSecret/TestUserPassword). Running `dotnet run --set-test-user-password`/`--seed` directly outside Docker, set your own local secrets once: dotnet user-secrets set "ClientSecret" "integration-test-secret" --project services/identity/src/Identity.Api && dotnet user-secrets set "TestUserPassword" "<your choice>" --project services/identity/src/Identity.Api. Neither is a RequiredSecret, so a bare `dotnet run` still starts the host without them — only --seed/--set-test-user-password read these, and each no-ops (not fails) if its value is missing.
